lines.text: In four days, Grand Theft Auto Six launches on PlayStation Five and Xbox Series X and S.
Sensor Tower estimates digital pre-orders have already passed a billion dollars. Take-Two hasn't confirmed that number. But its CEO says pre-orders are running far in excess of expectations.
And it isn't cheap. Seventy-nine ninety-nine for the standard edition. Ninety-nine ninety-nine for the Ultimate.
lines.say: And it isn't cheap. Seventy-nine ninety-nine for the standard version. Ninety-nine ninety-nine for the ultimate.

lines.text: Nobody outside Rockstar knows what it cost. Rockstar told Bloomberg it was not quite as much as the Burj Khalifa, a building estimated at one and a half billion dollars.
Rockstar now has more than four thousand seven hundred employees. Nearly double the headcount from when work began.
That's a bet you only make with a hit behind you. The series has sold half a billion copies. GTA Five alone, more than two hundred and thirty million.
Take-Two needs this. In the three months to September, its net bookings fell eighteen percent, to one point six billion dollars.
For October to December, it's guiding three point three five to three point five billion. More than double. Mostly on one game.
The CEO, Strauss Zelnick, is careful about it. Quote: we tend to avoid claiming success before it occurs.
Three things on launch day. Whether Xbox cloud streaming holds up when it opens at one A.M. Eastern. The thirty frames per second target on both consoles. And whether pre-orders turn into real sales.
Then the long game. Bloomberg reports GTA Online earned around half a billion dollars a year for GTA Five. The online mode for Six comes later.
That's the money behind the biggest launch of the year. Save your game.
